title: Tensor-stable cocones give Day-compatible presheaf relations
statement: Use the universes, monoidal infinity categories and coherent cocones of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Day convolution and local equivalences from [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. Fix a universe $\mathcal A$ and an auxiliary larger universe in which the categories below are formed. Let $C$ be an $\mathcal A$-small monoidal infinity category and let $R$ be an $\mathcal A$-small family of specified coherent cocones $r=(p:K\to C,\ p\to\Delta_K x)$ with $K$ an $\mathcal A$-small simplicial set; empty $K$ is allowed. Assume that for every $r\in R$ and $c\in C$, both tensor cocones $c\otimes r$ and $r\otimes c$ are equivalent as coherent cocones to members of $R$ (equivalence includes the diagram and its apex). Write $y:C\to P_{\mathcal A}(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal A})$ for Yoneda, and let $s_r:\operatorname{colim}_K yp\to y(x)$ be the arrow induced by $r$. Put $S_R=\{s_r:r\in R\}$. Then $S_R$ is monoidally compatible with Day convolution: for every $r\in R$ and $F\in P_{\mathcal A}(C)$, both $F\otimes_{\mathrm{Day}}s_r$ and $s_r\otimes_{\mathrm{Day}}F$ are $S_R$-local equivalences. No cocone in $R$ is assumed colimiting in $C$, and no existence of colimits in $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Definition 8.1 and Section 9 preceding Corollary 9.1: tensor compatibility of the localized-presheaf colimit relations. General tensor-stable-cocone formulation isolated from the agent argument of universe-embeddings step 3; online source, not archived. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
The monoidal Yoneda theorem makes $P_{\mathcal A}(C)$ presentable relative to $\mathcal A$, and Day convolution preserves $\mathcal A$-small colimits separately. For $r=(p:K\to C,p\to x)$ and $c\in C$, these properties and coherent strong monoidality identify the entire arrow
$$y(c)\otimes s_r\simeq\bigl(\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}y(c\otimes p(k))\longrightarrow y(c\otimes x)\bigr)=s_{c\otimes r}.$$
The identification respects the arrow because the cocone legs are sent by strong monoidal Yoneda to the tensor cocone legs, and the map out of the colimit is induced by those legs. An equivalence of coherent cocones, including their diagrams and apices, induces an equivalence of these arrows. Tensor stability therefore identifies this arrow with a member of $S_R$. Such an arrow is an $S_R$-local equivalence by the definition of locality. On the right the same calculation gives $s_r\otimes y(c)\simeq s_{r\otimes c}$, again an $S_R$-local equivalence. This includes $K=\varnothing$, since Day tensor preserves initial objects.

Choose the $\mathcal A$-small coherent density cocone $y\circ p_F\to F$, indexed by $E_F$, supplied by Yoneda density. Applying the coherent arrow-valued functor $G\mapsto G\otimes s_r$ gives a diagram of arrows $y(p_F(e))\otimes s_r$ and a cocone to $F\otimes s_r$. Its source and target cocones are colimiting because the functors $-\otimes\operatorname{colim}_K yp$ and $-\otimes y(x)$ preserve small colimits. The pointwise colimit theorem for $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,P_{\mathcal A}(C))$ therefore identifies this cocone as a colimit in the arrow infinity-category. All shapes used here are $\mathcal A$-small; no colimit in $C$ is used.

Apply the small-localization saturation theorem in the presentable category $P_{\mathcal A}(C)$ from Step 1, with the $\mathcal A$-small set $S_R$. Its mapping-space condition is exactly the definition of $S_R$-local equivalence. Hence the class of local equivalences equals the class generated by $S_R$ and equivalences under the closure operations in that theorem; in particular it is closed under $\mathcal A$-small colimits in the arrow category. Every arrow in the diagram of Step 2 is a local equivalence by Step 1. Its colimit $F\otimes s_r$ is therefore a local equivalence.

Apply the same density cocone to $G\mapsto s_r\otimes G$. Separate cocontinuity gives the source and target colimits, so the arrow-colimit theorem identifies
$$s_r\otimes F\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{e\in E_F}(s_r\otimes y(p_F(e)))$$
as an equivalence of arrows. The right-representable calculation of Step 1 uses the hypothesis on $r\otimes c$ and proves that every arrow in this diagram is local. The saturation closure from Step 3 makes its colimit local. Thus both tensor directions satisfy precisely the definition of monoidal compatibility. No symmetry is used.

lean.note: Uses normalized HomPresentation Yoneda, small underlying category and small arbitrary simplicial shapes, and actual tensor-image cocones. Stability is equivalence of entire coherent cocones with a compatible apex equivalence, including empty shapes.
